title: A ring beam in a drift tube in particle-in-cell: its space-charge depression and the limiting current
source: A thin annular electron beam of radius r_b in a grounded pipe of radius R, held on its lines by a strong axial magnetic field and injected at γ₀ through a grounded plane, slows to γ_b with I = I₀(γ₀ − γ_b)β_b/(2 ln(R/r_b)), I₀ = 4πε₀mc³/e = 17.045 kA; no more than the limiting current I_L = I₀(γ₀^{2/3} − 1)^{3/2}/(2 ln(R/r_b)) passes, the rest turned back by a virtual cathode (L. S. Bogdankevich, A. A. Rukhadze, Sov. Phys. Usp. 14:163, 1971; R. B. Miller, An Introduction to the Physics of Intense Charged Particle Beams, Plenum 1982, §3.2). γ₀ = 1.25 (127.75 keV), R = 10 mm, r_b = 6 mm: I_L = 1071.7 A; at 750 A, γ_b = 1.16166 (the faster root, by bisection). Evaluated apart from the code under test (CODATA 2018 constants)
